items.stem: On which dates were atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki?
items.answer: 6 and 9 August 1945

items.stem: Briefly explain why air power became decisive in the Second World War.
items.answer: Air superiority protected ground and naval forces (Battle of Britain, Midway), carriers replaced battleships as the key naval weapon, and strategic bombing damaged enemy industry and fuel supplies.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Air superiority protected ground and naval forces (Battle of Britain, Midway), carriers replaced battleships as the key naval weapon, and strategic bombing damaged enemy industry and fuel supplies. items.stem: Explain why the Battle of the Atlantic was crucial to Allied victory.
items.answer: Britain depended on imported food, fuel and munitions, and the US build-up for D-Day required safe convoys; by mid-1943 convoys, long-range aircraft, radar and Ultra intelligence defeated the U-boats.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Britain depended on imported food, fuel and munitions, and the US build-up for D-Day required safe convoys; by mid-1943 convoys, long-range aircraft, radar and Ultra intelligence defeated the U-boats. items.stem: A student claims that blitzkrieg was a carefully planned German strategy for winning the whole war quickly. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Many historians (e.g. Karl-Heinz Frieser) argue Blitzkrieg emerged improvisationally from operational success in 1940 rather than a pre-war master plan; it failed against the USSR in 1941.
items.markingKey: Many historians (e.g. Karl-Heinz Frieser) argue Blitzkrieg emerged improvisationally from operational success in 1940 rather than a pre-war master plan; it failed against the USSR in 1941. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why Blitzkrieg was successful against France in 1940.
items.answer: German armour advanced through the Ardennes, which the French thought impassable, and crossed the Meuse at Sedan; the Allies had spread their tanks in support of infantry and moved into Belgium, so the German thrust to the Channel cut off their best armies.

items.answer: The National Service (No. 2) Act

items.stem: Explain why civilians became targets in the Second World War.
items.answer: Total war blurred the line between soldier and civilian: bombing aimed to destroy production and morale, occupation regimes used terror against populations, and Nazi racial ideology led to genocide.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Total war blurred the line between soldier and civilian: bombing aimed to destroy production and morale, occupation regimes used terror against populations, and Nazi racial ideology led to genocide. items.stem: Explain the difference between the home front in Britain and the home front in the USSR.
items.answer: Britain mobilised through democratic consent with rationing and conscription and suffered bombing; the USSR relocated over 1,500 factories east of the Urals, imposed extreme labour discipline and suffered occupation and immense civilian losses.
items.markingKey: Britain mobilised through democratic consent with rationing and conscription and suffered bombing; the USSR relocated over 1,500 factories east of the Urals, imposed extreme labour discipline and suffered occupation and immense civilian losses. [Photograph] A milkman in a white coat steps over the rubble of a bombed London street carrying crates of milk bottles, while firemen hose down smoking ruins behind him.
— Description of a photograph by Fred Morley, published in British newspapers, October 1940

With reference to the origin, purpose and content of Source D, assess its values and limitations for historians investigating the home front in the Second World War. [3]
items.answer: Value: It shows how the British press presented civilian life during the Blitz and the image of resilience used to sustain morale. Limitations: The photograph was staged (Morley used a colleague as the milkman), so it is propaganda rather than a record of normal life; censorship hid panic and anger.

items.stem: Briefly describe the evacuation of Soviet industry (1941) and explain what it reveals about economic mobilisation on the home front.
items.answer: About 1,500 factories and millions of workers were moved east to the Urals and Siberia in 1941–42, where production resumed. The relocation allowed the USSR to out-produce Germany in tanks by 1943 despite losing its western industrial regions.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Non-Intervention Committee"?

The US strategy in the Pacific of capturing selected islands to build airbases while bypassing heavily defended Japanese positions
The treaties and agreements that end a war and determine territorial, political and economic arrangements, such as the Paris peace treaties of 1947
The committee set up in London in 1936 by Britain and France to prevent foreign intervention in Spain, which Germany, Italy and the USSR ignored

items.stem: Explain why the Nationalists won the Spanish Civil War.
items.answer: Franco had a unified command, the professional Army of Africa (airlifted by German and Italian planes), and substantial German and Italian aid; the Republic was divided between communists, socialists and anarchists (May Days 1937) and was hampered by non-intervention.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Franco had a unified command, the professional Army of Africa (airlifted by German and Italian planes), and substantial German and Italian aid; the Republic was divided between communists, socialists and anarchists (May Days 1937) and was hampered by non-intervention. items.stem: Ingrid writes: "The Spanish Republic lost because it had no foreign support." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The Republic received Soviet arms and the International Brigades, but this aid was smaller and less consistent than Axis aid, and the Republic’s internal divisions also mattered.
items.markingKey: The Republic received Soviet arms and the International Brigades, but this aid was smaller and less consistent than Axis aid, and the Republic’s internal divisions also mattered. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Source B
From Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic, an iron curtain has descended across the Continent. Behind that line lie all the capitals of the ancient states of Central and Eastern Europe, all subject in one form or another, not only to Soviet influence but to a very high and in some cases increasing measure of control from Moscow.
— Winston Churchill, speech at Westminster College, Fulton, Missouri, 5 March 1946 (extract)

With reference to the origin, purpose and content of Source B, assess its values and limitations for historians investigating the effects of 20th-century wars. [4]
items.answer: Value: It shows the perception of a leading Western statesman of the post-war division of Europe and was influential in shaping Western opinion. Limitations: Churchill was out of office and speaking to a US audience to encourage an Anglo-American alliance; it presents only the Western view.

items.stem: Lars writes: "The Long March was a great military victory for the CCP." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: It was a costly retreat in which about 90 per cent of those who set out died or deserted; its importance was political and symbolic, and it confirmed Mao’s leadership at Zunyi (1935).

items.stem: What was the code name for the German invasion of the USSR in June 1941?
items.answer: Operation Barbarossa

items.stem: Noah writes: "Women permanently replaced men in industry after 1945." Explain why this is inaccurate.

items.stem: "The Spanish Republic lost because it had no foreign support." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: The Republic received Soviet arms and the International Brigades, but this aid was smaller and less consistent than Axis aid, and the Republic’s internal divisions also mattered.
items.markingKey: The Republic received Soviet arms and the International Brigades, but this aid was smaller and less consistent than Axis aid, and the Republic’s internal divisions also mattered. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why the Spanish Civil War had long-lasting political effects in Spain.
items.answer: Franco established a dictatorship that lasted until his death in 1975, with repression of Republicans (tens of thousands executed after 1939), Catholic nationalism and suppression of regional identities such as Catalan and Basque.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Franco established a dictatorship that lasted until his death in 1975, with repression of Republicans (tens of thousands executed after 1939), Catholic nationalism and suppression of regional identities such as Catalan and Basque. items.stem: "The CCP won the civil war mainly because of Soviet military aid." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Soviet aid (notably Japanese weapons captured in Manchuria in 1945) helped, but Stalin gave limited support and even advised Mao to compromise; the CCP’s victory rested mainly on its own organisation, peasant support and GMD weakness.
items.markingKey: Soviet aid (notably Japanese weapons captured in Manchuria in 1945) helped, but Stalin gave limited support and even advised Mao to compromise; the CCP’s victory rested mainly on its own organisation, peasant support and GMD weakness. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Rafael writes: "Blitzkrieg was a carefully planned German strategy for winning the whole war quickly." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Many historians (e.g. Karl-Heinz Frieser) argue Blitzkrieg emerged improvisationally from operational success in 1940 rather than a pre-war master plan; it failed against the USSR in 1941.

items.stem: With reference to the partition of Korea (1945), explain how it illustrates the territorial effects of the Second World War.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against the view that the Second World War transformed the position of women in society.
items.answer: The war accelerated change in attitudes and opportunities, but much was temporary in the short term.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: conscription of women in Britain and combat roles in the USSR; women in industry (Rosie the Riveter); French women gained the vote in 1944. Arguments against: many returned to domestic roles after 1945; pay inequality persisted; Nazi Germany mobilised women less extensively. Supported judgement: The war accelerated change in attitudes and opportunities, but much was temporary in the short term.
